title: How an elevator stops itself from falling

lines.text: This is why an elevator almost never falls.
First, a shaft with guide rails running all the way up.
The car rides on those rails, so it can't sway.
It hangs from several steel ropes, and one can hold the car by itself.
Up top, a motor turns a grooved wheel.
A counterweight balances the car, about as heavy as the car forty percent full.
If the power goes out, springs clamp the motor's brake shut.
Next is the governor, spun by its own rope as the car moves.
If the car goes too fast, the governor grabs that rope.
That pulls steel wedges under the car tight against the rails.
At the bottom of the pit, buffers act like giant shock absorbers.
In eighteen fifty four, Elisha Otis stood on his safety elevator and had the ropes cut.
Would you ride one after the cable snapped?
